_comment: Transition validators workflow-apply.sh --rules ensures are present.
Additive only: a rule already on the transition (same ruleKey + parameters) is left alone, a missing one is appended, nothing is ever removed.
Transitions are matched by NAME. Parameter values may name a field or a status instead of a site id:
{field:<name>}  -> the custom field id, resolved via GET /field
{status:<name>} -> the status id, resolved via GET /statuses/search
Names are matched exactly and case-sensitively; a placeholder that resolves to zero or several matches is fatal.
Parameter shapes for both ruleKeys were recorded from live Jira Cloud responses: fixtures/workflows.bulkget.rules-after.txt.
Which work-order requirement each rule serves is stated in BINDING.md.
Triage is the entry state and deliberately carries NO validator: a ticket is not yet a contract there ([JIRA-13]).

Open is the ready-to-work position. To Do is its read-only alias ([JIRA-15]) and is never provisioned, so the To Do rule below applies only where the Jira project template already left that transition: the deferral automation uses it, and an ungated alias would be a way around the gate.

parameters.errorMessage: verify is required to leave triage for the ready-to-work position (work-order MUST-7, per JIRA-13)
verify is required to reach the ready-to-work position (work-order MUST-7, per JIRA-13)
defer_until is required to defer: without it nothing says when the ticket comes back (work-order MUST-47, per JIRA-14)
verify is required to defer, so the automation that returns this issue to To Do can satisfy that transition unattended (work-order MUST-7, per JIRA-14)
verify is required before work starts (work-order MUST-7)
touches is required before work starts (work-order MUST-13, tightened by JIRA-6)
verify is required before completing (work-order MUST-7)
outcome is required to cancel (work-order MUST-28)
